chapter: Buck's Legion band and later gigs
title: Buck's American Legion band, personnel and reeds, 14 and a half years
summary: Schiro joins the Legion band; personnel changes, Dan Tagnan's hard reeds, and the long-running job.

story.theme_name: Who was in the band: naming sidemen and personnel
story.community_name: Who played in the band: reciting personnel

blocks.x: Yeah, a lot of jokes and all we had. I mean, I don't remember them all. I mean, it was... Taiwan, no more. Yeah, then, uh... We had a marching band up around the end of the concert. We'd see boys through the park and all the crowd would follow us, you know? Yeah. Something like the Saints or High Society. It was a lot of fun. I learned a lot out there, too. Some people would dance and all? Yeah, they're dancing there, you know, listening and everything else. And then we had some dance music and some marches and some light overtures and so forth. Oh, yeah. And I played with Buck Banville there, the American League. That's the old Plumpland. Yeah, that's...yeah. That's the, uh, Gentilly Post night, 203, or the Johnny Link's Post. What was in the band when you started that? Oh, there was... Arthur Duffy, yeah, that's Buh-Boy, that's on drums. And Bob Aguilar on the piano. Henry Connect on trumpet. And Fred Dante on the sides. And... What did Buck play? Oh, he also played the trumpet. They had a couple of trumpets, the Henry Connect, then Buck, then, uh... You see, Bob Aguilar died. So, so, so, but...so I took over on the piano. In the meantime, Henry got sick. So we hired Arthur Bubert. And then, uh, in the meantime, Dan Tagnan died, so we hired Leach. And, uh, he and I used to team up nice. I could, I could never get along with Dan too much, because he was up and down the sides. He was mechanical. And, uh, I just... He was a fine-sex man. And he used to overpower me. I mean, I had a soft to read. He had about a five read. I had about a two and a half. And he said, what the hell you blow loud? I said, well, it's the best I can do, Dan.
And he'd just get all frustrated. Can you still buy another five read? Do they still make them that hard?
No, I don't believe. I doubt it.
I never have known anybody that played a five read. Yeah.

It's a real hard read. Oh, I don't know how you did it. A four or three and a half, or three is, you know, average. I mean, if it might be set to have, no, you don't have to have those hard reads. Yeah. When I came... The layers are different. Yeah.
Do they have wider lay nouns?
Yeah, they're wider layers. You have to use a soft to read them. It all depends on the man behind it, too.
Yeah, well, I guess a wide lay would give you a bigger tone. Yeah, bigger tone, though. I don't know. But, let's see, about 1950 was when I first came out there.
Yeah, Otto Bubert was on trumpet, fine trumpet man. And, uh...
Roland was on alto. Yeah, alto.

Roland Lee. And we had Charlie Fabry on drums. That's right. He also died. And then, uh... Well, we had a few substitutes like Buster, you got on drums. I don't know him. Well, I mean, he was a fine, you know, drummer. And then they had, you see, the three Mike Lawlers, I mean, each other had some good. A little black mic and a red mic. And also, old man Jack Assunto, a trombone. He played a few... And a lot of leaders, you know, tried to get that job by the time we grew up in the Union, but we had the job sewed up for 14 and a half years.
Well, I knew that job wouldn't last, though.
